title: Advanced Single Candles
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/0/title: Marubozu: the candle with no wicks
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/0/body: A **Marubozu** is a candle with almost **no wicks at all**: it's all body. A bullish marubozu opens at the low and closes at the high, so buyers had **full control** from start to finish. The bearish one is the reverse.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/0/tip: In practice, tiny wicks are fine too. What matters is that the body fills almost the whole candle.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/1/body: A **doji** means the open and close are nearly the same. A **long-legged doji** has long wicks on both sides, a **Dragonfly** has only a long lower wick, and a **Gravestone** has only a long upper wick.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: After a few hours of chop, what kind of candle is the last one?
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/2/explanatio: A long green body with no real wicks: price opened near the low and closed at the high. Buyers owned the whole period.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/3/statement: A bearish marubozu means price opened near the high and closed near the low.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/3/explanatio: With no wicks, the open is the high and the close is the low. Sellers pushed price down from start to finish.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/4/title: A doji means doubt, not reversal
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/4/body: A doji on its own isn't a buy or sell signal. It only says buyers and sellers are in **balance**. It gains meaning **after a long move** or at a **key level**, and even then you should wait for the **next candle**.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/4/tip: A dragonfly at the end of a downtrend and a gravestone at the top of an uptrend are the most meaningful cases.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/5/explanatio: This candle opened and closed near its low with a long upper wick: buyers pushed price up, but by the close it was all taken back. Price dropped right after.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: After this drop, what is the last candle (a dragonfly doji) telling you?
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/options/0/: Sellers pushed price down, but buyers brought it back
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/options/1/: Buyers had full control from start to finish
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/options/2/: Sellers closed price at the very low
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/options/3/: The drop is now certain to continue
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/7/explanatio: A long lower wick means sellers dragged price down, but buyers pulled it back to the open by the close. That's a warning for the downtrend; wait for a confirmation candle before you enter.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/8/sentence: In a bullish marubozu, the open is the candle's ___ and the close is the candle's ___.
lessons/candles-u2-l1/steps/8/explanatio: A bullish marubozu has no wicks, so it opens at the lowest price of the period and closes at the highest.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/0/body: An **inverted hammer** has a small body at the bottom and a **long upper wick**, and it shows up **after a downtrend**. Buyers pushed price up for the first time. They couldn't hold it yet, but selling pressure is fading.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/0/tip: The inverted hammer is a weaker signal, so always wait for a confirmation candle.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/1/body: A **hanging man** looks exactly like a hammer (body on top, long lower wick), but it shows up **at the top of an uptrend**. Its long wick shows sellers dragged price way down mid-period: the first warning that **buyers are weakening**.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: After this downtrend, what pattern is the last candle?
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/2/explanatio: A small body at the bottom and a long upper wick, at the end of a downtrend: an inverted hammer. The same shape at the top of an uptrend would be a shooting star.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: What about this one? The last candle formed after a rally.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/3/explanatio: It's shaped like a hammer, but it came at the top of an uptrend. So it's a hanging man: a warning that buyers are weakening, not a buy signal.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/4/statement: The hammer and the hanging man have the same shape; the only difference is where they appear.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/4/explanatio: Both have a small body on top and a long lower wick. At the end of a downtrend it's a hammer; at the top of an uptrend it's a hanging man.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/5/body: These two patterns aren't enough on their own. **Confirmation** means the next candle proves the pattern's direction: after a hanging man, a candle **closes below its body**; after an inverted hammer, a candle **closes above its body**.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/6/prompt: There are two hammer-shaped candles on this chart. Tap the hanging man.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/6/explanatio: The candle at the bottom came after a drop, so it's a hammer. The one that formed after the rally, at the top of the trend, is the hanging man. Notice price fell right after it.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: After a rally, a hanging man formed and the next candle closed below its body. What's the most sensible choice?
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/7/explanatio: The hanging man gave a warning and the next bearish candle confirmed it: sellers are taking control. A pullback is now more likely, but not certain. Put your stop loss above the hanging man's high.
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/prompt: You spot an inverted hammer after a downtrend. What should the next candle do to confirm it?
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/options/0: Close above the inverted hammer's body
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/options/1: Close below the inverted hammer's low
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/options/2: Be a tiny doji in the middle of the body
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/options/3: Close exactly at the inverted hammer's low
lessons/candles-u2-l2/steps/8/explanatio: Confirmation means buyers keep going and the next candle closes above the body. A close below its low means the pattern failed.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/0/body: In candlestick reading, **shape alone isn't enough**. A candle with a long lower wick is a **hammer** at the end of a downtrend and a **hanging man** at the top of an uptrend. The inverted hammer and shooting star work the same way. First look at **what trend came before**.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/1/body: A hammer **on support** or a shooting star **under resistance** is worth far more than the same pattern in the middle of nowhere. The key level shows **why** buyers or sellers stepped in there.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/1/tip: The best setups are where several reasons line up: trend, level and pattern.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/2/options/0: One that formed on strong support after a drop
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/2/options/1: One that formed in the middle of a small, choppy range
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/2/options/2: One that formed mid-uptrend, far from any level
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/2/options/3: No difference; all three are worth the same
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/2/explanatio: A hammer is a reversal pattern. It's strongest after a drop, at a level buyers have defended before.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/3/prompt: There are two hammer-like candles here. Tap the one that formed in the right place (on support).
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/3/explanatio: The second hammer formed right on the 2340 support, where buyers had turned price around before. The first one was mid-move, and price kept falling after it.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/4/statement: A shooting star in the middle of a small, aimless range is worth just as much as one under major resistance.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/4/explanatio: Inside a range, price keeps bouncing up and down and these shapes pop up all the time. Under major resistance, the same pattern shows sellers are really defending that level.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/5/body: A pattern also gives you your **entry and stop loss**. For a hammer: enter after confirmation, above the hammer's high, with the **stop loss just below the hammer's low**. If that low breaks, the reason for the trade is gone.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/6/prompt: Bitcoin came back to the 58,000 support, printed a hammer, and the next candle closed green. What do you do?
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/6/explanatio: The hammer formed on a support that had turned price around before, and the next candle confirmed it. A move up is more likely, but not guaranteed. Stop loss below the hammer's low.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/7/prompt: Why is this hammer a weak buy signal?
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/7/options/0/: There was no trend before it and it's not at a key level
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/7/options/1/: Its lower wick is too long
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/7/explanatio: The market is ranging, and this hammer came neither after a drop nor at the bottom of the range. It's in the middle. The same shape at the range low would have been worth much more.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/prompt: Put the steps of trading a candlestick pattern in order.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/items/0: Identify the prior trend and the key level
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/items/1: Wait for the pattern to form at that level
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/items/2: Wait for the next candle to confirm it
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/items/3: Enter and place your stop beyond the pattern's wick
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/8/explanatio: Context first, then the pattern, then confirmation, and finally an entry with a clear stop loss. Flip the order and you'll end up chasing every shape you see.
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/prompt: After a long drop, gold reached the 2300 support and printed a high-volume hammer right there. The next candle closed above the hammer's high. What's the best read?
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/options/0: A reversal is more likely; you can buy with a stop below the hammer
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/options/1: The reversal is certain; no stop loss needed
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/options/2: You should sell, since the prior trend was down
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/options/3: A hammer on support tells us nothing
lessons/candles-u2-l3/steps/9/explanatio: Prior trend, key level, pattern, volume and confirmation all point the same way. That's a quality setup. But no pattern is certain, so you still need a stop below the hammer's low.
